llm.reply:
Cystic fibrosis is linked in the knowledge graph to the CF transmembrane conductance regulator gene [1], as well as to Fc gamma receptor IIa [3] and transforming growth factor beta 1 [4], alongside the disease record itself [2].

## Gene Associations

The core disease-causing gene is CF transmembrane conductance regulator, NCBIGene:1080 [1]. Fc gamma receptor IIa, NCBIGene:2212 [3], and transforming growth factor beta 1, NCBIGene:7040 [4], are also associated, consistent with roles as modifier genes influencing disease severity or complications rather than the primary cause.

## Clinical Picture

The MedGen record for cystic fibrosis lists clinical features including asthma [11], bronchiectasis [15], clubbing of fingers [19], dehydration [23], diarrhea [27], hemoptysis [28], hepatomegaly [29], and hepatosplenomegaly [30], reflecting the multisystem nature of the disease.

## Literature Context

Supporting literature covers complications and management, including a report that hyperammonemic encephalopathy can arise in cystic fibrosis liver disease and be triggered by factors such as systemic corticosteroids [26: "hyperammonemic encephalopathy can be precipitated in previously stable CFLD by various triggers including systemic corticosteroids"], as well as editorials on cystic fibrosis-related diabetes [22] and cystic fibrosis in children [14], and papers on azithromycin use [18] and nutrition [10] in the disease.

The knowledge graph links cystic fibrosis to the genes NCBIGene:1080, NCBIGene:2212, and NCBIGene:7040 as associated with the disease record for Cystic fibrosis [1][3][4][2].

## Gene Identities

NCBIGene:1080 is annotated as CF transmembrane conductance regulator [1]. NCBIGene:2212 is annotated as Fc gamma receptor IIa [3]. NCBIGene:7040 is annotated as transforming growth factor beta 1 [4].

## Disease And Literature Indexing

The disease is indexed in MedGen under the title Cystic fibrosis [6], and as a literature entity under the name Cystic Fibrosis [7]. Associated clinical features recorded for this concept include Asthma [11], Bronchiectasis [15], Clubbing of fingers [19], Dehydration [23], Diarrhea [27], Hemoptysis [28], Hepatomegaly [29], and Hepatosplenomegaly [30].

## Related Publications

Indexed publications on cystic fibrosis include one titled Encephalopathy in cystic fibrosis [5], carrying PubMed ID 32800451 [9], whose abstract describes a rare hyperammonemic encephalopathy complication that can be precipitated by triggers including systemic corticosteroids in patients with stable cystic fibrosis liver disease [26: "hyperammonemic encephalopathy\" can be precipitated in previously stable CFLD by various triggers including systemic corticosteroids"]. Other indexed titles include 3.22 Nutrition in Cystic Fibrosis [10], Editorial: Cystic Fibrosis in Children with PubMed ID 35240644 [14][13], Azithromycin and cystic fibrosis with PubMed ID 35592838 [18][17], Editorial: Cystic fibrosis-related diabetes with PubMed ID 35853636 [22][21], and a further publication carrying PubMed ID 39129918 [25].

## Related Trials

Registered clinical trials on the topic include Assessment of Quadriceps Muscle Electrostimulation Used in Patients Suffering From Cystic Fibrosis [8] and Pregnancies and Cystic Fibrosis [24]. Other trials retrieved for the surrounding search, concerning fibrocystic breast conditions rather than cystic fibrosis itself, include A Study of Topical Danazol for the Treatment of Pain Associated With Fibrocystic Breast Disease [12], Efficacy and Safety of ONCOXIN in Patients With Breast Fibrocystic Disease [16], and A Clinical Study on the Efficacy and Safety of the Treatment of Hyperplasia of Mammary Glands With Xiaoru Sanjie Capsule [20].
